probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the

condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

Other human F values for lipophilic basic drugs are ≥32% (naratriptan 63–74%, netupitant >60%/63–87%, encainide 76–78% in cirrhosis, LSD 80%, silodosin 32.2%, SXB 88%, sulpiride ~35% with a 10–70% range); no affirmative human F<20% record for query-like esters is present.

L5 bidirectional permeability records for other molecules show high Papp and efflux ratios ≤1.1 (SUVN-G3031 ER 0.81; trihexyphenidyl ER 0.22; fexofenadine dispersion ER 1.10; compound 5v ER 1.0), supporting favorable absorptive transport and no gut-wall efflux liability, but they are not direct F measurements for the query. Several L5 cards are duplicate records of the same measurements and are not independent.
The only sub-20% records are non-query animal data (silodosin rat F 9.2% and compound III rabbit F 13.4 ± 6.5%); they are not transferable to the query and do not affirm F<20%.
